served.stem: The passage supports each of the following statements EXCEPT
choices: Some of the fungi that form mycorrhizas produce mushrooms on a forest floor
Fungi steer carbon toward the seedlings most closely related to the donor
Phosphate moves through soil slowly enough to leave a root short of it
There are plants that live without making any sugar of their own
A share of what a tree makes in a given week ends up in fungal tissue
served.bankWhy: Paragraph 14 raises a return to a relative only as one of the things a donor would need to get back for the behaviour to persist. The passage never reports that fungi actually route carbon by kinship, and paragraph 13 says flow may be set by the fungus or by simple demand.

passage.title: The Trade Beneath the Forest Floor

distractorNotes: Paragraph 4 supports this by naming boletes, amanitas, chanterelles and truffles as ectomycorrhizal fungi.
Paragraph 5 supports this: phosphate diffuses so slowly that a root creates its own depletion zone within days.
Paragraph 15 supports this with ghost pipe and a number of orchids, which make no sugar at all.
Paragraph 8 supports this with the girdling result, which shows the fungi living on sugar made that week.

answer.text: Fungi steer carbon toward the seedlings most closely related to the donor
answer.line: Relatives come up once, in paragraph 14, as a payback evolution would need. No line says fungi steer carbon by kinship.

steps: Flip the job. Four choices have a line behind them; you are hunting the one that does not.
Check off four: mushrooms in paragraph 4, slow phosphate in paragraph 5, sugar made that week in paragraph 8, plants that make no sugar in paragraph 15.
Look hard at the one left. A relative appears only in paragraph 14, as one thing a donor would need back. A condition, not a finding.
Paragraph 13 even says flow may be set by the fungus, or simply by which end is hungrier.
